### Managing student details
#### Adding a student: `add`
Format: `add n/NAME p/PHONE addr/ADDRESS l/LEVEL sub/SUBJECT`
All five fields are required:
| Field | What you can enter |

| `n/NAME` | 1–100 characters: letters, spaces, apostrophes, hyphens, periods and slashes. At least one letter; no digits. Letters from other languages are accepted. Extra spaces are reduced to one. |

| `p/PHONE` | Exactly 8 digits (`0`–`9`). Spaces, including copied non-breaking spaces, are removed: `9123 4567` becomes `91234567`. Do not include `+65`, country codes, hyphens or invisible zero-width characters. |
| `addr/ADDRESS` | 1–200 characters of meaningful text; not just spaces or invisible characters. Use `addr/`, **not** `a/`. |
| `l/LEVEL` | 1–40 characters: English letters, digits and spaces. For example, `Sec 3`, `JC1` or `Sec 4 Normal Academic`. Brackets and hyphens are not allowed. |

| `sub/SUBJECT` | 1–50 characters: English letters, digits, spaces, hyphens, `&`, `(`, `)`, `+` and commas. Start with an English letter or digit. For example, `E-Math` or `E-Math & A-Math`; slashes are not allowed. |
A student with both the same phone and the same name as another student is rejected, ignoring name case and extra spaces. Equal names with different phones are allowed.
Only the five listed markers start fields. Other slash text stays in the preceding value: `n/Amy t/friend` saves the name `Amy t/friend`, while `sub/Math t/friend` makes the subject invalid.
Examples:
- `add n/Tan Wei Ming p/87654321 addr/Blk 8 Bishan St 22, #05-13 l/JC1 sub/H2 Math`
- `add n/Ramesh s/o Kumar p/9123 4567 addr/12 Clementi Rd l/Sec 3 sub/Physics`
**Screenshot:** `add n/Jamie Lee p/81230007 addr/60 Example Street l/JC1 sub/Physics` adds Jamie at the end of the list.
#### Editing a student: `edit`
Format: `edit INDEX [n/NAME] [p/PHONE] [addr/ADDRESS] [l/LEVEL] [sub/SUBJECT]`

Give at least one field. Only supplied details change, following the [add rules](#adding-a-student-add), including duplicate checks. Lesson records and flags are kept. After success, everyone is listed again and the edited student opens on the right.
Examples:
- `edit 1 p/91234567` changes student 1's phone.
- `edit 1 n/Muthu a/l Raju` changes only the name, keeping the address.
- `edit 2 l/Sec 4 sub/A-Math` changes student 2's level and subject.
**Screenshot:** `edit 1 l/Sec 4 sub/A-Math` updates Alex Tan's card and details.
#### Deleting a student: `delete`
Format: `delete INDEX`

Removes the student at that number in the current list, **including all their lessons and their flag**. Deletion is saved automatically and cannot be undone in the app. Check the student's number in the list currently shown. To choose from everyone, enter `list` first, then check the number again.
**Screenshot:** starting from the six-student list above, `delete 2` removes Priya Ramesh. Marcus Lim becomes student 2.
### Lesson records

Student numbers always refer to the current student list. Lesson numbers come from `view STUDENT_INDEX`: **lesson 1 is the newest**, and records without dates appear last. Before changing a lesson, run `view` again if you have recorded, deleted or redated lessons since checking its number.
#### Logging a lesson: `loglesson`
Format: `loglesson INDEX c/CONTENT [date/DATE]`
Records what you taught. The date is today unless you supply `date/`:

- `CONTENT` is 1–300 characters of meaningful text, not just spaces or invisible characters. Internal spacing and characters used in real text are kept. Follow the [slash guidance](#using-commands) for `c/` and `date/` inside notes.

- Use `DD/MM/YYYY`, for example `21/10/2026`; single-digit days and months such as `1/2/2026` also work. The year must have four digits. Dates must exist and be from **01/01/2000 up to today** on your computer. Future dates are rejected.
- A backdated lesson appears in its date position. For the same date, the most recently logged appears first. Logging identical content twice creates two records.
- The confirmation shows the student, date and content. Use `editlesson` to correct it or `deletelesson` to remove it. The current student list and flags are kept.
Examples:
- `loglesson 1 c/Electric circuits: series and parallel, Q1-5 for homework`
- `loglesson 2 c/Surds and indices date/20/10/2026`
**Screenshot:** after `list`, `loglesson 1 c/Trigonometry: solved right-angled triangle problems. date/18/10/2026` records an earlier lesson for Alex Tan.
#### Viewing a student's lesson records: `view`
Format: `view INDEX`
Opens the student's details and complete lesson history on the right, and lists their records in the result box. Viewing changes no saved details or student search.
- Records are numbered newest date first. For example, `1. 18/10/2026: Quadratic inequalities`. Older records without dates show `(undated)` after the dated records. Repeated entries remain separate.
- With no lessons, the message is `No lessons logged yet for NAME.`, and the details panel suggests a `loglesson` command.
- You can also click a student card. After clicking the list, use Up, Down, Page Up, Page Down, Home or End to view another student. This keeps any command you are typing.
##### The details panel

`view`, `findlesson`, `loglesson`, `edit`, `editlesson`, `deletelesson`, `flag` and `unflag` open the student they act on, with their latest details. Other commands, including `add`, keep the current student open while they remain in the displayed list. Filtering them out or deleting them clears the panel; failed commands keep it unchanged. After `unflag` in a flagged-only list, the unflagged student leaves the list but stays open so you can see the change.
At startup, nobody is selected. The panel suggests `view 1`, `list` or an `add` command according to whether students are visible, hidden by a search, or absent.
#### Searching a student's lessons: `findlesson`
Format: `findlesson INDEX [KEYWORDS] [from/DATE] [to/DATE]`
Find a topic, a date range, or both for one student:
- Give at least one keyword or date boundary. Put all keywords **before** `from/` and `to/`; give each boundary at most once, in either order.
- All keywords must occur in the lesson content, in any order. Part of a word works, ignoring case. Punctuation is matched as typed; wildcards and spelling correction are not supported.

- Dates use the format and earliest date described under `loglesson`. Future search dates are allowed. Both boundary dates are included; leave one out for an open-ended range. `from/` cannot be later than `to/`; equal dates search a single day.
- When both content and dates are supplied, all must match. Records without dates can match content searches, but are excluded whenever a date boundary is supplied.
- Matching lessons keep their numbers from the **complete history**: results 2 and 4 stay
numbered 2 and 4. `findlesson` does not take a lesson number. Use the returned numbers with
`editlesson` or `deletelesson`, and check again after any lesson changes.
- The matches appear only in the result box. The details panel shows the student's **complete** history, and the student list is unchanged. The search is not remembered.
- No matches gives `No matching lesson records found for NAME.`; no lessons gives
`No lessons logged yet for NAME.` Search content without `c/`: use `findlesson 1 algebra`.
If a search using `c/` or `date/` finds no matches, TutorLah explains the supported format.
Examples:
- `findlesson 2 algebra` searches lesson content.
- `findlesson 2 from/01/10/2026 to/31/10/2026` searches October's dated records.
- `findlesson 2 revision from/01/10/2026` searches revision records from 1 October onwards.
**Screenshot:** `findlesson 1 algebra from/01/10/2026 to/31/10/2026` finds Amy Tan's lessons 2 and 4. Her full history remains on the right.
alt="Two matching Algebra lessons for Amy Tan, retaining full-history lesson numbers 2 and 4"
#### Editing a lesson record: `editlesson`
Format: `editlesson STUDENT_INDEX LESSON_INDEX [c/CONTENT] [date/DATE]`
Give content, a date, or both, using the same limits as `loglesson`. The student, other lessons, flags and current student list are kept.
- Omitted fields keep their values. Give at least one field; unchanged content and date gives `The lesson already has those details.`

- A content-only edit keeps the lesson number. Changing its date moves it into date order and **may change its number**. The confirmation gives the new number; on a shared date, the moved lesson appears first among that date's records.
- An undated lesson stays undated unless you supply a date. You cannot remove a date from a dated lesson.
Examples:
- `editlesson 2 1 c/Quadratic inequalities and homework review` corrects lesson 1 for student 2.
- If `view 1` shows Trigonometry (23/10/2026), Vectors (21/10/2026) and Algebra (19/10/2026), `editlesson 1 3 date/22/10/2026` moves Algebra from lesson 3 to lesson 2.
#### Deleting a lesson record: `deletelesson`
Format: `deletelesson STUDENT_INDEX LESSON_INDEX`

Deletes just that lesson. The student, their flag, other records and the current student list are kept. Even identical lessons are separate records; only the chosen one is removed. Remaining lessons are renumbered from 1. Removing the final lesson keeps the student with no lessons.
Use exactly two positive whole numbers without leading zeros. Missing or extra values show
the command format. Numbers such as `0`, `01` or an unavailable number give a student- or
lesson-index error. With no lessons, the message is `No lessons logged yet for NAME.`
**Deletion cannot be undone in the app.**
**Screenshots:** after the logging example, `view 1` shows Alex's four lessons; Trigonometry is lesson 2.
Enter `deletelesson 1 2` to remove it. Alex and the other three lessons remain.
### Follow-up flags
#### Flagging students for follow-up: `flag`
Format: `flag INDEX [r/REASON]`
Marks a student needing follow-up. Their card and details show a red flag; the details panel shows the reason or `Flagged (no reason given)`.

- A reason is optional. If given, use 1–100 characters after removing surrounding spaces; it cannot be blank or contain only invisible characters. Pasted tabs and line breaks become spaces in the command box; other control characters cannot be part of a reason.
- Only `r/` is recognised as a field, so reasons can contain text such as `a/level`, `date/` or `c/homework`.
- Flagging again with a different reason replaces the reason. The same reason gives an already-flagged message. Omitting `r/` keeps an existing reason and reports that the student is already flagged.
- Flags are saved and kept when you edit student details or change lessons.
**Screenshot:** `flag 1 r/Missed homework twice` marks Alex Tan and shows the reason.
#### Removing a flag: `unflag`
Format: `unflag INDEX`
Removes the flag and reason. If the student is not flagged, TutorLah says so. Both `flag` and `unflag` use the current displayed number and open the student on the right.
Example: `unflag 2` removes student 2's flag and its reason.
#### Listing flagged students: `flagged`
Format: `flagged`

Shows all flagged students, replacing any previous student search. Results keep their original order and are numbered from 1; use those displayed numbers in other commands. If none are flagged, TutorLah suggests `list`.

Example: enter `flagged`, then `unflag 1` to resolve the first displayed student's follow-up. The student leaves the flagged-only list but stays open on the right without a flag. Use `list` to show everyone. Extra text is rejected, and the flagged-only view is not kept after restarting.

## Using the window

Drag the divider below the result box to give long results more room, or scroll inside it. Each command starts its feedback at the top. Drag the divider between the student list and details panel to adjust their widths; scroll inside the details panel for a long history.
The window can shrink to 700 × 420 pixels and opens no larger than your primary screen. If a saved position no longer fits on a connected screen, TutorLah opens in the center of the primary screen.
## Keeping your data safe
### Saving and backups
TutorLah saves automatically after a successful change. Viewing, searching, showing totals, help and exit do not save or change student records.

Your students, lessons and flags are in `data/addressbook.json` inside the folder you launch TutorLah from. With Quick start, the `data` folder sits beside `TutorLah.jar`. **Close TutorLah before copying this file to a safe location as a backup.** Sample students are not saved until you first change data.

Only one copy can use the same data folder at a time. If a second copy reports a conflict, close the first before trying again. A leftover hidden `.tutorlah.lock` file is harmless and does not mean TutorLah is still running.
### If saving fails

The failed change is canceled: your students, lessons and displayed list return to their previous state. Check the reported file location, folder permissions and available disk space, fix the problem, then retry. Do not assume the failed command was saved. The previous saved file is kept if writing or replacing it fails; a failed first save leaves no empty student file.
Saving also needs a folder that supports replacing a file in one step.
### If your saved students cannot be opened

TutorLah shows a warning with the file's location and a short reason, then opens with an empty student list. **Saving is disabled to protect the original file.** Commands that only read data still work, but changes cannot be saved.
1. Close TutorLah.
1. Make a backup of the file named in the warning.
1. Restore a valid backup at that location, or correct the file using the advanced notes below.
1. Restart TutorLah. Repairing the file while the app remains open does not enable saving.
### Advanced: editing the saved file
<panel header="Optional file-editing details" expanded>

Use the commands above for normal updates. If you edit `data/addressbook.json` directly, close TutorLah and make a backup first. The file uses **JSON**, a text format with named fields and brackets. Keep it as UTF-8 text without a byte-order mark (BOM), which some editors add at the beginning.
- Keep one complete outer object with all students inside it. Do not join two data files together or add text after the closing `}`; only spaces or line breaks may follow it.

- Student fields follow the [add rules](#adding-a-student-add). Phones in the file must already be exactly eight digits, without spaces. Names are tidied before checking duplicates; duplicates make the whole file unreadable rather than being merged.

- Lesson dates are stored as `"date": "YYYY-MM-DD"`, for example `"date": "2026-10-18"`. Missing dates mean undated lessons. Dates before `2000-01-01`, impossible dates and other formats are rejected. Existing future dates still load in case your computer clock changed; recording or changing a date through commands still rejects future dates.

- Lessons display newest first, with undated records last. For records with the same date, or without dates, the last entry in the file appears first. Repeated records are kept. After editing the file, use `view` to check the lesson numbers before changing a record.
- A flag with a reason uses `"flag": {"reason": "REASON"}`; one without a reason uses `"flag": {}`. An unflagged student has no `flag` field. Older files without flags still load.

- Blank or invisible-only addresses, lesson content and flag reasons are invalid. An invalid file produces the protected recovery state described above; the warning may mention JSON and a line and column to help locate the problem.

If saving fails, follow [If saving fails](#if-saving-fails). After a forced shutdown, hidden `.tutorlah-*.tmp` files may remain. TutorLah does not use or remove them on restart. Close all copies before deleting these temporary files; keep `addressbook.json` and `preferences.json`.
</panel>
## FAQ
**How do I transfer my data to another computer?**
1. Install Java and download TutorLah on the new computer, following Quick start.
1. Close TutorLah on both computers.

1. Copy the old `data/addressbook.json` to a `data` folder inside the new launch folder. Create the folder if needed; back up any existing destination file before replacing it. Do not combine the files.
1. Start TutorLah from the new folder. Use `list` and `view INDEX` to check that students, lessons and flags have loaded.
## Known issues
- **Minimized Help window:** if the Help window is minimized, running `help`, choosing Help from the menu or pressing F1 does not restore it. Restore the existing window manually.

- **Fullscreen on macOS:** if TutorLah is in fullscreen mode, the Help window opens in its own fullscreen space instead of over TutorLah. Pressing F1 again does not bring it back, and it keeps opening in fullscreen even after TutorLah leaves fullscreen mode. The Help window only links to this User Guide, so use this guide directly instead.

output instead of answering from memory, and confirm a path exists
before giving it.

Command words, indexes and prefix boundaries accept Unicode whitespace,
including non-breaking spaces. Trim surrounding field whitespace but keep
meaningful internal spacing and joiners. Pasted tabs and line breaks become
spaces before the command box removes them; pasting never executes a command.
| Field | Prefix | Accepted | Invalid-value message |

| Name | `n/` | 1 to 100 characters after collapsing repeated spaces. Unicode letters, spaces, `'`, `-`, `.` and `/`, with at least one letter. No digits. | `Names should be 1 to 100 characters long, contain at least one letter, and use only letters, spaces, apostrophes, hyphens, periods and slashes.` |
| Phone | `p/` | Exactly 8 ASCII digits after removing Unicode whitespace. No `+` or country code. | `Phone numbers should be exactly 8 digits.` |
| Address | `addr/` | 1 to 200 printable characters | `Addresses must not be blank and must be at most 200 characters.` |
| Level | `l/` | 1 to 40 characters: English letters (A-Z, a-z), digits 0 to 9, spaces (#211) | `Levels should be 1 to 40 characters long and use only English letters, digits 0 to 9 and spaces.` |

| Subject | `sub/` | 1 to 50 characters, starting with an English letter or digit: English letters (A-Z, a-z), digits 0 to 9, spaces, hyphens, `&`, `(`, `)`, `+`, commas (#211) | `Subjects should be 1 to 50 characters long, start with an English letter or a digit 0 to 9, and use only English letters, digits 0 to 9, spaces, hyphens, &, (, ), + and commas.` |
| Lesson content | `c/` | 1 to 300 printable characters, internal spaces kept | `Lesson content must not be blank and must be at most 300 characters.` |

| Lesson date | `date/` | Optional. A real date as `D/M/YYYY` or `DD/MM/YYYY` (digits only, four-digit year), from 01/01/2000 (`Lesson.EARLIEST_DATE`), not in the future | `Lesson dates should be real dates from 01/01/2000 onwards, in the format DD/MM/YYYY, for example 21/10/2026.` |

| Flag reason | `r/` | Optional. 1 to 100 characters after trimming surrounding Unicode whitespace; not blank and no control characters | `Flag reasons must not be blank and must be at most 100 characters.` |
- `ParserUtil#parsePhone` removes Unicode `White_Space` in `add` and `edit`,
including non-breaking and narrow non-breaking spaces. Zero-width formatting
characters are not removed. JSON phone values still require eight ASCII digits
without whitespace; storage does not use command-input normalization.
- Addresses and lesson content cannot consist entirely of Unicode whitespace
or format characters, including non-breaking spaces, ZERO WIDTH SPACE
(U+200B), WORD JOINER (U+2060) and BOM (U+FEFF). The model validators enforce
this for typed commands and JSON loading, with the same messages above.
Real text keeps internal spaces and formatting, including joiners used by
written languages and emoji sequences.
- `/` is allowed in names so that `s/o` and `d/o` work. No prefix starts
with `s/`, `o/` or `d/`. `date/` is used only by `loglesson`, so lesson content
such as `d/dx` and names such as `d/o` are unaffected.

- **Address prefix `addr/` (#109):** the address prefix is `addr/`, not `a/`, so names containing `a/l` or `a/p` (e.g. `Muthu a/l Raju`) are kept in full by `add` and `edit`, and `edit` never changes the address through a name. When `addr/` is missing and ` a/` appears, `add` appends `The address prefix is addr/, for example addr/1 Example Street.` to its usage message.
- **Duplicate student:** same phone, and names equal when case is ignored
(`Person#isSamePerson`).

## 5. Agreed Java interfaces (as on `master`)

- `JsonUtil#fromJsonString` reads exactly one JSON value, allowing only whitespace after it. Extra root values and malformed trailing content are JSON parse failures. Student-file loading then uses the existing sanitized recovery warning and save guard; the ignored suffix is never discarded by a later save. Preferences use the same strict reader and retain their existing fallback policy. `"guiSettings": null` is also treated as an unreadable preferences file, so startup uses the defaults instead of failing (#209).

- `LogicManager` saves student data only when it differs from the snapshot taken before command execution. Read-only commands and edits that leave stored values unchanged skip saving, so help, exit and filters still work during recovery or write failures. First-run sample data is saved by the first data-changing command.

- Save permission errors name `Storage#getAddressBookFilePath`, never the temporary path from the exception. Other filesystem errors use `Could not save data to file {PATH} due to the following error: {REASON}`, using only `FileSystemException#getReason`; null or blank reasons use `The file or folder could not be written.`. Other IO errors retain their existing messages, including the saving-disabled explanation. The original exception remains the cause, and rollback and temporary-file cleanup are unchanged.

- `Model#getFilteredPersonListPredicate()` captures the active student filter as a non-null predicate. `LogicManager` snapshots the address book and filter before command execution. If saving fails, it restores changed student data and the captured filter before throwing the existing save-error `CommandException`. Lesson records and flags are preserved, and later commands cannot silently save the failed mutation.

- If reading a student data file fails (including a null JSON root or null student entry), that `JsonAddressBookStorage` instance refuses every later save with `MESSAGE_SAVE_BLOCKED`: `Saving is disabled because the student data file could not be loaded. Close TutorLah, repair or restore the file, then restart.` `MainApp` starts with an empty model and `UiManager` shows a recovery warning including the file location and a sanitized `Reason:`. A non-blank `IllegalValueException` message is retained. A JSON syntax error, including one wrapped by Jackson mapping, gives `Reason: The file is not valid JSON (line N, column M).` when both coordinates are positive, or `Reason: The file is not valid JSON.` otherwise. Invalid structures and other errors give `Reason: Check that the file is readable and contains valid student data.` Raw parser messages, JSON excerpts and internal class names are not displayed. The original student file is preserved. Read-only commands still work; changed student data is rejected by the guard and rolled back. From the course guidance on [functionality bugs][bugs] and
[feature flaws][flaws]. A PE tester judges the app by what a reasonable

# TutorLah: context
Last updated: Oct 28, 2026, for find search suggestions (#187) and case-insensitive command words (#185).
Do not update the "Last updated" line in feature PRs; keeping it stable avoids
merge conflicts between concurrent branches.
## What it is
TutorLah is a desktop app for freelance tutors in Singapore who teach secondary
and junior college (JC) students one-to-one. They use it to keep student
details and record what each lesson covered. It is built by
adapting AddressBook-Level3 (AB3), the SE-EDU sample app, and keeps AB3's
architecture and typing-first workflow while reshaping the data and commands
around tutoring.
## Who it's for
Jaren is a full-time freelance tutor in Singapore with about 18 one-to-one
students from Sec 1 to JC2, in subjects such as A-Math, Physics and H2
Chemistry. He teaches at their homes, travels between
lessons on a tight schedule, and keeps everything on one laptop. His notes are
split between a spiral notebook and WhatsApp chats with parents, so each lesson
starts with working out where the last one stopped. He prefers typing to
clicking.
## Why AB3 is a good base
AB3 is already a typing-first desktop app for managing a list of people.
Jaren's core need has the same shape: a list of students he picks by number and
acts on with short commands. The work is adapting who is stored and what is
recorded about them, not building a new kind of app.
## What changes from AB3
| | AB3 | TutorLah |
| **Entity** | `Person` (a contact) | Student |
| **Fields** | name, phone, email, address, tags | name, phone, address, **level**, **subject**, and an optional follow-up **flag** with an optional reason. Email and tags are not in the spec. |
| **Name rule** | letters and digits only (`[\p{Alnum}][\p{Alnum} ]*`) | Unicode letters, spaces, `'` `-` `.` `/`, with no digits, so names like Mary-Anne, O'Brien and Ramesh s/o Kumar work |

| **Level and subject rules** | not in AB3 | English letters (A-Z, a-z), digits 0 to 9 and spaces, up to 40 characters for a level and 50 for a subject. Subjects also allow `-` `&` `(` `)` `+` and commas, and start with an English letter or a digit 0 to 9. Other scripts, such as Chinese or Tamil, are not accepted (#211). |
| **Phone rule** | digits only, at least 3 | exactly 8 digits, since every Singapore number is 8 digits and a fixed length catches typos |
| **Duplicate** | same name (`isSamePerson`) | same phone **and** same name ignoring case, since two students can both be "Tan Wei Ming" |
| **`list`** | ignores any extra text | rejects parameters; reports `Listed {COUNT} students.` (`Listed 1 student.` for one) or `No students found. Use add to create a student.` |
| **New entity** | none | **Lesson**: a record of what was covered and the date it was logged, owned by a student |
| **New commands** | none | Lesson commands plus `flag INDEX [r/REASON]`, `unflag INDEX` and `flagged` |
## What stays from AB3
- **Architecture:** UI, Logic, Model and Storage, connected through interfaces.
- **Choosing by index:** `delete 3` targets the 3rd *displayed* student, the
same as AB3's commands.
- **Command style:** a case-insensitive command word, an index, then lowercase
`prefix/value` parameters
in any order.
- **Storage:** JSON on disk. AB3 currently saves to `data/addressbook.json`.

TutorLah allows only one running copy per data folder. It keeps an operating-system lock on `data/.tutorlah.lock` for the whole session; a second copy explains the conflict and exits before loading or changing student data.

If a command cannot be saved, TutorLah restores its preceding in-memory student data and active filter, then reports the save error. Retrying uses the original displayed indexes; a later command cannot silently persist a failed mutation.

Save permission and filesystem errors identify the configured student data file instead of a hidden temporary file. Filesystem failures show their reason, such as a full disk, without including staging paths. The original exception remains available for diagnostics, and the existing rollback and cleanup behaviour is kept.

If an existing student file cannot be loaded, including a null JSON root or null student entry, the app shows recovery instructions and disables saving for that session. Commands cannot overwrite the unreadable file. Read-only commands, help and exit still work; a data-changing command is rejected and rolled back. The tutor exits, backs up and repairs or restores the file, then restarts to resume normal use. A genuinely missing file still loads sample students. Student data is saved only when a command changes it, so read-only commands do not rewrite the file.

When loading student data, names use the same whitespace normalization as commands before identity checks. Equivalent names with the same phone make the file invalid; students and their records are never silently merged. Imported lessons are stably sorted oldest first, with undated lessons before dated lessons in storage and saved order kept for equal dates. Dates before 01/01/2000 are rejected, while undated legacy records and existing future dates are retained so a clock correction cannot invalidate saved records. Command-side future-date checks remain unchanged. A failed load shows a field-validation reason or a short JSON syntax explanation with line and column when known. Invalid structures and other read problems get general recovery guidance. The dialog does not quote student data or internal exception details. Loading and read-only commands do not rewrite the original bytes.

Student data and preferences are serialized completely, written to a unique temporary file beside the destination and replaced atomically. A write or replacement failure keeps the previous saved file; failed first saves leave no empty destination. Temporary files are cleaned up where possible. Abrupt termination may leave a hidden `.tutorlah-*.tmp` file that is not loaded or cleaned up on restart; it can be removed after closing all copies of TutorLah. Unsupported atomic replacement is a save error, with no non-atomic fallback. This does not add a second-instance lock or guarantee recovery from power loss.
## Where the changes land in the code

Saved JSON files contain exactly one root value followed only by whitespace. Extra values or malformed trailing content are rejected. An invalid student file enters protected recovery, preserving its original bytes; invalid preferences retain the existing default-preferences fallback. Null GUI settings count as invalid preferences (#209).
- **Model:** the `Person` fields change, `Level` and `Subject` are added, the
duplicate rule changes, a `Lesson` list sits on each student, and an optional
immutable `Flag` records follow-up state.
- **Logic:** `AddCommandParser` gets new prefixes (`l/`, `sub/`), and there are
new `LogCommand` and `ViewCommand` classes with their parsers. `list` gets
a check that rejects parameters.
- **Storage:** `JsonAdaptedPerson` saves level, subject, lessons and optional flags.
- **UI (#155):** a split view. The left list has compact cards: displayed index,
initials, name, `level · subject`, lesson count/latest date, and a red flag icon
for flagged students. The right details panel shows one student's level and
subject chips, phone, address, flag reason banner and numbered lessons, newest
first, with the same numbers as `view`. Tutors can type `view INDEX` or
left-click a student card to open that student, while command text is preserved.
The click callback uses the current displayed index and the existing command path.
`view`, `findlesson`, `loglesson`, `edit`, `editlesson`, `deletelesson`, `flag` and
`unflag` open their student in the panel through `CommandResult#getStudent`.
Other commands keep the panel's student while it is still displayed, and clear
the panel otherwise. Failed commands turn the result box red and never change
the panel. Successful views highlight the matching card and scroll it into view.
Card presses are handled before selection updates, so switching from typed
commands needs only one click. `view` still lists the records in the result box.
With no student selected, the panel suggests `view 1`, `list` or the `add` format,
whichever works for the current list. The window can shrink to 700 x 420 pixels
and opens no larger than the primary screen, for 1280x720 displays at 150%
scale. Its saved position is kept when the complete window fits on a connected
screen, including a negative-coordinate secondary screen. An obsolete or
off-screen position is replaced by a centred position on the primary screen.
The README, website home page and User Guide share `docs/images/Ui.png`,
a screenshot of the current GUI using fictional student and lesson details.
Main-window guide screenshots use a 1488 x 846 pixel canvas and a 726 pixel
display width. `Ui.png` keeps that display width but is taller, so that six
students and a full lesson history fit. The help dialog links to the User
Guide with a Copy URL button, without individual command hints, and keeps its
natural proportions. Captures show the application window with its title bar,
without mouse or assistant overlays.
Addresses and lesson content cannot consist only of Unicode whitespace or
formatting characters, such as non-breaking spaces and zero-width spaces.
Commands and JSON loading use the same validation. Real text keeps its
internal spaces and formatting, including joiners used in written languages
and emoji sequences.
Command words, indexes and prefixed fields can be separated by Unicode
whitespace, including non-breaking spaces. Pasted tabs and line breaks become
spaces so words do not join. Tutors check the pasted command and press Enter
to run it; meaningful spacing inside addresses and lesson content is kept.
A prefix the command uses always starts a new field after whitespace, so text
such as `c/o` or `date/time` cannot appear after whitespace inside lesson notes. Tutors reword
it (`care of`, `date and time`); the duplicate-field and `loglesson`/`editlesson`
date errors say so. This is a deliberate, documented limitation.
`add` and `edit` remove Unicode whitespace, including non-breaking spaces,
from phone values before checking for exactly eight ASCII digits. Zero-width
characters remain invalid. Stored phone values must already be eight digits;
loading does not normalize them.
For invalid `add` phones, levels and subjects, a separate prefix-like token
after an otherwise valid value adds guidance listing the supported fields.
Names and addresses keep their normal errors. No extra fields are parsed.

| Delete a lesson | `deletelesson STUDENT_INDEX LESSON_INDEX` | `deletelesson 2 1` |

| Command | Format | Example |

`findlesson` searches one displayed student's lesson content, an inclusive date
range or both. Every keyword must match; date searches exclude undated lessons.
Keywords must precede date prefixes; extra words after a valid date get a correction example.
Results keep their original `view` numbers for editing or deletion, but those
numbers can change after a lesson mutation. The search is a one-off result and
changes neither stored data nor the student filter.
When a lesson search finds no matches for keywords starting with `c/` or `date/`,
the feedback explains date boundaries and plain content keywords. Searches still
match literal text; no hint is added to successful results or empty histories.

`summary` counts all students and all lesson occurrences, even when `find` or `flagged` filters the visible list. It keeps that filter and shows a single short paragraph explaining the totals. Cards show a lesson count and the most recent recorded date, or `No lessons yet` / `N lessons (undated)` where appropriate. The line refreshes when lesson records change. These values are derived from existing data and introduce no JSON fields.
Flags mark unresolved follow-up without changing student identity or lesson
history. The reason is optional and can be replaced by flagging again with a
different reason. `flagged` replaces the current filter and `list` restores all
students. Flag state is persisted; filter state is not.
`edit` changes only the fields given and keeps the student's lesson records.
`deletelesson` removes one record using the lesson number shown by `view`
(newest first). The student and their other lesson records are kept.
The confirmation includes the lesson date, or `(undated)` for a legacy record.
An empty history reports `No lessons logged yet for NAME.`.
Added in v1.5:
| Command | Format | Example |
| Edit a lesson | `editlesson STUDENT_INDEX LESSON_INDEX [c/CONTENT] [date/DATE]` | `editlesson 2 1 c/Vectors date/21/10/2026` |

`editlesson` corrects one lesson's content, date or both, using the lesson number shown by `view`. A content-only edit keeps the lesson's number. A new date moves the lesson into date order, so the confirmation gives its new number.
`find` shows students whose name, subject and level contain every keyword
given for that field, ignoring case and keyword order; partial words are
accepted. Bare keywords and `n/` search names, `sub/` subjects and `l/`
levels, and every given field must match, so a tutor can bring up all Sec 3
Physics students at once. It searches all students each time and uses literal
keywords without spelling correction. Every word after `sub/` or `l/` belongs
to that field, so names go first; if a search such as `find sub/Physics ng`
finds no one but `find ng sub/Physics` would, TutorLah suggests that search
without changing the list (#187).
Results keep their original order and are renumbered from 1. Commands and
card clicks use these displayed indexes. `list` restores the full list.
Adding or editing also restores it; viewing, logging and deleting students
or lessons retain the filter. Searching changes no student or lesson data,
and filters are not kept across restarts.
Case-insensitive search compares substrings directly rather than lowercasing
names and keywords separately, so Greek sigma variants also match. An empty
student panel offers both `list` and the add-command format and example,
covering searches with no matches as well as a genuinely empty address book.
`loglesson` dates each lesson with today's date (v1.4, issue #98), or with
`date/DD/MM/YYYY` for a lesson taught earlier (issue #120). Future dates are
rejected. `view` shows each record as `NUMBER. DD/MM/YYYY: CONTENT`, most
recent date first. Lessons saved before v1.4 have no date and show
`(undated)`. The data file stores the date as `YYYY-MM-DD`.
## Scope
- **In the MVP:** add, delete, list, log a lesson, view lessons.
- **Added in v1.4:** edit a student's details (lessons are kept), find
students by partial name, delete individual lesson records, and date
each logged lesson.
- **Added in v1.5:** persistent follow-up flags with optional reasons and a
filtered flagged-student view, editing a lesson record's content or date, and
student/lesson totals with per-student lesson status, and lesson-history search.
- **Planned next:** parent or guardian contact,
weekly slots, homework tracking, rescheduling, monthly lesson counts,
archiving.
- **Out of scope:** arranging lessons, messaging parents, grading, payments,
exam planning, and moving data between machines.
## Decisions (Oct 8, 2026)
- **No lesson date** in the MVP. `log` takes content only. Replaced in v1.4
by issue #98: `log` dates each lesson with today's date. `log` was renamed
`loglesson` on Oct 29 (#227), to match the other lesson commands.
- **View order:** most recently logged first (reverse logging order), as
agreed by the team on Oct 8. Implemented in PR #63. This replaces the
earlier order-logged proposal. Since issue #120, lessons are kept in date
order, so `view` shows the most recent date first.
- **Email and tags are removed.** They may return post-MVP as optional
fields.
- **`edit`, `find` and `clear` are removed for the MVP** and can be restored
from Git history later. Removed from the code in issue #72 (Oct 14).
`edit` was restored in issue #100 (Oct 20) for v1.4.
`find` was restored in issue #101 (Oct 20), with all-keyword partial matching, and extended to subject and level in issue #143 (Oct 25); `clear` remains removed.
- **`view` replaces `lessons`** as the command for viewing a student's lessons.
- **`/` is allowed in names** so that s/o and d/o work. Since #109 (Oct 26)
the address prefix is `addr/`, so `a/l` and `a/p` names such as
`Muthu a/l Raju` also work in `add` and `edit`.
- **Duplicates** are the same phone with the same name ignoring case.
## Shared index policy
- **Invalid index messages:** `delete`, `loglesson`, and `view` accept positive
integers without leading zeros. There is no arbitrary 1000 cap. Zero,
negative integers, leading-zero integers, values too large to parse, and
indexes outside the displayed list give "The student index provided is
invalid." Missing or malformed command parts keep the command's invalid
format message and usage.
For coding agents, use `tutorlah-agent-brief.md`, which has the full rules,
messages and interfaces.
